title: Recording with Tatum
summary: Roy says Tatum accompanied well in clubs but took over the record date, and Moon Song recalled the Alley sessions.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Well, some people say that Art was a great solo pianist, but he wasn't very good at accompanying people and so on.

Oh, they don't know that... Well, I enjoyed playing with him. Not so much the record we made, because once he was in that studio, it was a different thing. When we used to go in the Alley and play, man, he'd play things behind me, you know. But on the record date, the minute the red light went on, man, he struck out, and we made that thing... "Can't I had a little Dance." I could hardly play the melody, he was ...(?)... find something!

I remember him playing once... It was a place uptown, like a social club or something, and he was there, and Charlie Shavers and a bunch of other guys. They were all sitting on the floor while Art was playing, and Art said to Charlie, "Any note you play, I'll play figure eights around it" -- you know, like a skater.
But on that record, though, there's some really nice,
relaxed things on it, too, like "Moon Song."

Well, see, "Moon Song is one of the things we used to play in Val's In The Alley. See? We was trying to recapture what we used to do back there. And that's the closest we got to it, "Moon Song" -- because I hadn't played that since then, since we were doing the thing in the Alley. Yeah, it was nice.
